name: accelerate
summary: A pattern of numbers that speed up (or slow down) samples while they play. Currently only supported by osc / superdirt.

name: adsr
summary: ADSR envelope: Combination of Attack, Decay, Sustain, and Release.

name: almostAlways
summary: Shorthand for .sometimesBy(0.9, fn)

name: almostNever
summary: Shorthand for .sometimesBy(0.1, fn)

name: always
summary: Shorthand for .sometimesBy(1, fn) (always calls fn)

name: amp
summary: Like gain, but linear.

name: anchor
summary: The top note to align the voicing to. Defaults to c5

name: appBoth
summary: When this method is called on a pattern of functions, it matches its haps with those in the given pattern of values. A new pattern is returned, with each matching value applied to the corresponding function. In this _appBoth variant, where timespans of the function and value haps are not the same but do intersect, the resulting hap has a timespan of the intersection. This applies to both the part and the whole timespan.

name: appLeft
summary: As with appBoth, but the whole timespan is not the intersection, but the timespan from the function of patterns that this method is called on. In practice, this means that the pattern structure, including onsets, are preserved from the pattern of functions (often referred to as the left hand or inner pattern).

name: apply
summary: Like layer, but with a single function:

name: appRight
summary: As with appLeft, but whole timespans are instead taken from the pattern of values, i.e. structure is preserved from the right hand/outer pattern.

name: appWhole
summary: Assumes 'this' is a pattern of functions, and given a function to resolve wholes, applies a given pattern of values to that pattern of functions.

name: arp
summary: Selects indices in in stacked notes.

name: arpWith
summary: Selects indices in in stacked notes.

name: arrange
summary: Allows to arrange multiple patterns together over multiple cycles. Takes a variable number of arrays with two elements specifying the number of cycles and the pattern to use.

name: as
summary: Sets properties in a batch.

name: asym
summary: Asymmetrical diode distortion

name: attack
summary: Amplitude envelope attack time: Specifies how long it takes for the sound to reach its peak value, relative to the onset.

name: bank
summary: Select the sound bank to use. To be used together with s. The bank name (+ "_") will be prepended to the value of s.
examples: s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").bank('RolandTR909') // = s("RolandTR909_bd RolandTR909_sd")

name: beat
summary: creates a structure pattern from divisions of a cycle especially useful for creating rhythms

name: begin
summary: A pattern of numbers from 0 to 1. Skips the beginning of each sample, e.g. 0.25 to cut off the first quarter from each sample.

name: berlin
summary: Generates a continuous pattern of [berlin noise](conceived by Jame Coyne and Jade Rowland as a joke but turned out to be surprisingly cool and useful, like perlin noise but with sawtooth waves), in the range 0..1.

name: binary
summary: Creates a binary pattern from a number.

name: binaryL
summary: Creates a binary list pattern from a number.

name: binaryN
summary: Creates a binary pattern from a number, padded to n bits long.

name: binaryNL
summary: Creates a binary list pattern from a number, padded to n bits long.

name: bite
summary: Splits a pattern into the given number of slices, and plays them according to a pattern of slice numbers. Similar to slice, but slices up patterns rather than sound samples.

name: bmod
summary: Modulates with the output from a given bus. Can be called in sequence like pat.bmod(...).bmod(...) to set up multiple modulators Send to an audio bus with otherPat.bus(..). There are two ways to declare which control will be modulated: 1. Explicitly put control in the config (e.g. bmod({ id: 2, c: "lpf" })) 2. If the control parameter is absent, the control _immediately before_ the bmod call will be used (e.g. s("saw").lpf(500).bmod({ id: 2 }) to modulate lpf) Modulators can be referred to by id so that they can be updated later e.g. inside a sometimes. See example below.

name: bpattack
summary: Sets the attack duration for the bandpass filter envelope.

name: bpdc
summary: DC offset of the LFO for the bandpass filter

name: bpdecay
summary: Sets the decay duration for the bandpass filter envelope.

name: bpdepth
summary: Depth of the LFO for the bandpass filter

name: bpdepthfrequency
summary: Depth of the LFO for the bandpass filter, in HZ

name: bpenv
summary: Sets the bandpass filter envelope modulation depth.

name: bpf
summary: Sets the center frequency of the band-pass filter. When using mininotation, you can also optionally supply the 'bpq' parameter separated by ':'.

name: bpq
summary: Sets the band-pass q-factor (resonance).

name: bprate
summary: Rate of the LFO for the bandpass filter

name: bprelease
summary: Sets the release time for the bandpass filter envelope.

name: bpshape
summary: Shape of the LFO for the bandpass filter

name: bpskew
summary: Skew of the LFO for the bandpass filter

name: bpsustain
summary: Sets the sustain amplitude for the bandpass filter envelope.

name: bpsync
summary: Cycle-synced rate of the LFO for the bandpass filter

name: brak
summary: Returns a new pattern where every other cycle is played once, twice as fast, and offset in time by one quarter of a cycle. Creates a kind of breakbeat feel.

name: brand
summary: A continuous pattern of 0 or 1 (binary random)

name: brandBy
summary: A continuous pattern of 0 or 1 (binary random), with a probability for the value being 1

name: bus
summary: A bus is a send which can be used for mixing patterns. It combines with.. s("bus") to play that bus through another pattern (for, say, applying non-linear effects like distortion to multiple signals) otherPat.bmod(..) (to modulate another pattern with the bus)

name: busgain
summary: Postgain multiplier prior to sending the signal to the audio bus.

name: byteBeatExpression
summary: Create byte beats with custom expressions

name: byteBeatStartTime
summary: Create byte beats with custom expressions

name: cat
summary: The given items are concatenated, where each one takes one cycle.

name: ccn
summary: MIDI control number: Sends a MIDI control change message.

name: ccv
summary: MIDI control value: Sends a MIDI control change message.

name: ceil
summary: Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values set to their mathematical ceiling. E.g. 3.2 replaced with 4, and -4.2 replaced with -4.

name: channel
summary: Choose the channel the pattern is sent to in superdirt

name: channels
summary: Allows you to set the output channels on the interface

name: chebyshev
summary: Distortion via Chebyshev polynomials

name: choose
summary: Chooses randomly from the given list of elements.

name: chooseCycles
summary: Picks one of the elements at random each cycle.

name: chooseInWith
summary: As with {chooseWith}, but the structure comes from the chosen values, rather than the pattern you're using to choose with.

name: chooseWith
summary: Choose from the list of values (or patterns of values) using the given pattern of numbers, which should be in the range of 0..1

name: chop
summary: Cuts each sample into the given number of parts, allowing you to explore a technique known as 'granular synthesis'. It turns a pattern of samples into a pattern of parts of samples.
examples:
samples({ rhodes: 'https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/132/132051_316502-lq.mp3' })
s("rhodes")
 .chop(4)
 .rev() // reverse order of chops
 .loopAt(2) // fit sample into 2 cycles

name: chord
summary: The chord to voice
examples: chord("<Am C D F Am E Am E>").voicing()

name: chorus
summary: mix control for the chorus effect

name: chunk
summary: Divides a pattern into a given number of parts, then cycles through those parts in turn, applying the given function to each part in turn (one part per cycle).

name: chunkBack
summary: Like chunk, but cycles through the parts in reverse order. Known as chunk' in tidalcycles

name: chunkBackInto
summary: Like chunkInto, but moves backwards through the chunks.
examples:
sound("bd sd ht lt bd - cp lt").chunkInto(4, hurry(2))
  .bank("tr909")

name: chunkInto
summary: Like chunk, but the function is applied to a looped subcycle of the source pattern.
examples:
sound("bd sd ht lt bd - cp lt").chunkInto(4, hurry(2))
  .bank("tr909")

name: clip
summary: Multiplies the duration with the given number. Also cuts samples off at the end if they exceed the duration.

name: coarse
summary: Fake-resampling for lowering the sample rate. Caution: This effect seems to only work in chromium based browsers

name: color
summary: Sets the color of the hap in visualizations like pianoroll or highlighting.

name: compress
summary: Compress each cycle into the given timespan, leaving a gap
examples:
cat(
  s("bd sd").compress(.25,.75),
  s("~ bd sd ~")
)

name: compressor
summary: Dynamics Compressor. The params are compressor("threshold:ratio:knee:attack:release") More info [here](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/DynamicsCompressorNode?retiredLocale=de#instance_properties)

name: constructor
summary: Create a pattern. As an end user, you will most likely not create a Pattern directly.

name: contract
summary: *Experimental* Contracts the step size of the pattern by the given factor. See also expand.

name: control
summary: MIDI control: Sends a MIDI control change message.

name: cosine
summary: A cosine signal between 0 and 1.

name: cosine2
summary: A cosine signal between -1 and 1 (like cosine, but bipolar).

name: cpm
summary: Plays the pattern at the given cycles per minute.

name: crush
summary: Bit crusher effect.

name: cubic
summary: Cubic polynomial distortion

name: cut
summary: In the style of classic drum-machines, cut will stop a playing sample as soon as another samples with in same cutgroup is to be played. An example would be an open hi-hat followed by a closed one, essentially muting the open.

name: cyclesPer
summary: A pattern measuring the duration of events, in cycles per event. cyclesPer doesn't have structure itself, but takes structure, and therefore event durations, from the pattern that it is combined with. For example cyclesPer.struct("1 1 [1 1] 1") would give the same as "0.25 0.25 [0.125 0.125] 0.25". See also its reciprocal, per, also known as perCycle.
examples:
sound("bd sd [bd bd] sd*4 [- sd] [bd [bd bd]]")
  .note(cyclesPer.add(20))

name: decay
summary: Amplitude envelope decay time: the time it takes after the attack time to reach the sustain level. Note that the decay is only audible if the sustain value is lower than 1.

name: defragmentHaps
summary: Combines adjacent haps with the same value and whole. Only intended for use in tests.

name: degrade
summary: Randomly removes 50% of events from the pattern. Shorthand for .degradeBy(0.5)

name: degradeBy
summary: Randomly removes events from the pattern by a given amount. 0 = 0% chance of removal 1 = 100% chance of removal

name: delay
summary: Sets the level of the delay signal. When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'delaytime' and 'delayfeedback' parameter, separated by ':'.

name: delayfeedback
summary: Sets the level of the signal that is fed back into the delay. Caution: Values >= 1 will result in a signal that gets louder and louder! Don't do it

name: delayspeed
summary: Sets the time of the delay effect.

name: delaysync
summary: Sets the time of the delay effect in cycles.

name: density
summary: Noise crackle density

name: detune
summary: Set detune for stacked voices of supported oscillators
examples: note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").detune("<.1 .2 .5 24.1>")

name: dictionary
summary: Which dictionary to use for the voicings. This falls back to the default dictionary if not provided
examples:
addVoicings('house', {
'': ['7 12 16', '0 7 16', '4 7 12'],
'm': ['0 3 7']
})
chord("<Am C D F Am E Am E>")
.dict('house').anchor(66)
.voicing().room(.5)

name: diode
summary: Diode-emulating distortion

name: discreteOnly
summary: Returns a new pattern, with 'continuous' haps (those without 'whole' timespans) removed from query results.

name: distort
summary: Wave shaping distortion. CAUTION: it can get loud. Second option in optional array syntax (ex: ".9:.5") applies a postgain to the output. Third option sets the waveshaping type. Most useful values are usually between 0 and 10 (depending on source gain). If you are feeling adventurous, you can turn it up to 11 and beyond ;)

name: distorttype
summary: Type of waveshaping distortion to apply.
examples:
s("sine").note("F1*2").release(1)
  .penv(24).pdecay(0.05)
  .distort(rand.range(1, 8))
  .distorttype("<fold chebyshev scurve diode asym sinefold>")

name: distortvol
summary: Postgain for waveshaping distortion.

name: djf
summary: DJ filter, below 0.5 is low pass filter, above is high pass filter.

name: drive
summary: Filter overdrive for supported filter types
examples: note("{f g g c d a a#}%16".sub(17)).s("supersaw").lpenv(8).lpf(150).lpq(.8).ftype('ladder').drive("<.5 4>")

name: drop
summary: *Experimental* Drops the given number of steps from a pattern. A positive number will drop steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

name: dry
summary: Set dryness of reverb. See room and size for more information about reverb.

name: duckattack
summary: The time required for the ducked signal(s) to return to their normal volume. Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. duckonset("0:0.003"). Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. duckorbit("2:3").

name: duckdepth
summary: The amount of ducking applied to target orbit Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. duckdepth("0.3:0.1"). Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. duckorbit("2:3").

name: duckonset
summary: The time required for the ducked signal(s) to reach their lowest volume. Can be used to prevent clicking or for creative rhythmic effects. Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. duckonset("0:0.003"). Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. duckorbit("2:3").
examples:
// Rhythmic
noise: s("pink").distort("2:1").orbit(4) // used rhythmically with 0.3 onset below
hhat: s("hh*16").orbit(7)
ducker: s("bd*4").bank("tr909").duckorbit("4:7").duckonset("0.3:0.003").duckattack(0.25)

name: duckorbit
summary: Modulate the amplitude of an orbit to create a "sidechain" like effect. Can be applied to multiple orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. duckorbit("2:3")

name: duration
summary: Sets the duration of the event in cycles. Similar to clip / legato, it also cuts samples off at the end if they exceed the duration.

name: early
summary: Nudge a pattern to start earlier in time. Equivalent of Tidal's <~ operator

name: echo
summary: Superimpose and offset multiple times, gradually decreasing the velocity

name: echoWith
summary: Superimpose and offset multiple times, applying the given function each time.

name: end
summary: The same as .begin, but cuts off the end off each sample.

name: env
summary: Configures an envelope. Can be called in sequence like pat.env(...).env(...) to set up multiple envelopes There are two ways to declare which control will be modulated: 1. Explicitly put control in the config (e.g. env({ c: "lpf" })) 2. If the control parameter is absent, the control _immediately before_ the env call will be used (e.g. s("saw").lpf(500).env({ a: 1 }) to modulate lpf) Modulators can be referred to by id so that they can be updated later e.g. inside a sometimes. See example below.
examples:
s("pulse").lpf(500).env({ a: 1 })
  .env({ c: "s", a: 1 })
  .diode(0.3)
  .sometimes(x => x.env({ a: "0.5" }, 1)) // envelope #1 (0-indexed)

s("pulse").lpf(500).env({ a: 1 }, 'lpf_mod')
  .env({ c: "s", a: 1 })
  .diode(0.3)
  .sometimes(x => x.env({ a: "0.5" }, 'lpf_mod'))

name: euclid
summary: Changes the structure of the pattern to form an Euclidean rhythm. Euclidean rhythms are rhythms obtained using the greatest common divisor of two numbers. They were described in 2004 by Godfried Toussaint, a Canadian computer scientist. Euclidean rhythms are really useful for computer/algorithmic music because they can describe a large number of rhythms with a couple of numbers.

name: euclidish
summary: A 'euclid' variant with an additional parameter that morphs the resulting rhythm from 0 (no morphing) to 1 (completely 'even'). For example sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,0) would be the same as sound("bd").euclid(3,8), and sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,1) would be the same as sound("bd bd bd"). sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,0.5) would have a groove somewhere between. Inspired by the work of Malcom Braff.

name: euclidLegato
summary: Similar to euclid, but each pulse is held until the next pulse, so there will be no gaps.

name: euclidLegatoRot
summary: Similar to euclid, but each pulse is held until the next pulse, so there will be no gaps, and has an additional parameter for 'rotating' the resulting sequence

name: euclidRot
summary: Like euclid, but has an additional parameter for 'rotating' the resulting sequence.
examples:
// A Samba rhythm necklace from Brazil
note("c3").euclidRot(3,16,14)

name: every
summary: An alias for firstOf

name: expand
summary: *Experimental* Expands the step size of the pattern by the given factor.

name: extend
summary: *Experimental* extend is similar to fast in that it increases its density, but it also increases the step count accordingly. So stepcat("a b".extend(2), "c d") would be the same as "a b a b c d", whereas stepcat("a b".fast(2), "c d") would be the same as "[a b] [a b] c d".
examples:
stepcat(
  sound("bd bd - cp").extend(2),
  sound("bd - sd -")
).pace(8)

name: fanchor
summary: controls the center of the filter envelope. 0 is unipolar positive, .5 is bipolar, 1 is unipolar negative
examples:
note("{f g g c d a a#}%8").s("sawtooth").lpf("{1000}%2")
.lpenv(8).fanchor("<0 .5 1>")

name: fast
summary: Speed up a pattern by the given factor. Used by "*" in mini notation.
examples: s("bd hh sd hh").fast(2) // s("[bd hh sd hh]*2")

name: fastChunk
summary: Like chunk, but the cycles of the source pattern aren't repeated for each set of chunks.

name: fastGap
summary: speeds up a pattern like fast, but rather than it playing multiple times as fast would it instead leaves a gap in the remaining space of the cycle. For example, the following will play the sound pattern "bd sn" only once but compressed into the first half of the cycle, i.e. twice as fast.

name: filter
summary: Filters haps using the given function

name: filterHaps
summary: Returns a new Pattern, which only returns haps that meet the given test.

name: filterValues
summary: As with filterHaps, but the function is applied to values inside haps.
examples:
const drums = s("bd sd bd sd")
kick: drums.filterValues((v) => v.s === 'bd').duck(2)
snare: drums.filterValues((v) => v.s === 'sd')
bass: s("saw!4").note("G#1").lpf(80).lpenv(4).orbit(2)

name: filterWhen
summary: Filters haps by their begin time

name: firstCycle
summary: Queries the pattern for the first cycle, returning Haps. Mainly of use when debugging a pattern.

name: firstOf
summary: Applies the given function every n cycles, starting from the first cycle.

name: fit
summary: Makes the sample fit its event duration. Good for rhythmical loops like drum breaks. Similar to loopAt.

name: floor
summary: Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values set to their mathematical floor. E.g. 3.7 replaced with to 3, and -4.2 replaced with -5.

name: fmap
summary: see withValue

name: fmattack
summary: Attack time for the FM envelope: time it takes to reach maximum modulation A number may be added afterwards to control the attack of the envelope of any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmatt5)
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmattack("<0 .05 .1 .2>")
._scope()

name: fmdecay
summary: Decay time for the FM envelope: seconds until the sustain level is reached after the attack phase. A number may be added afterwards to control the decay of the envelope of any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmdec6)
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmdecay("<.01 .05 .1 .2>")
.fmsustain(.4)
._scope()

name: fmenv
summary: Ramp type of fm envelope. Exp might be a bit broken.. A number may be added afterwards to control the envelope of any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmenv4)
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmdecay(.2)
.fmsustain(0)
.fmenv("<exp lin>")
._scope()

name: fmh
summary: Sets the Frequency Modulation Harmonicity Ratio. Controls the timbre of the sound. Whole numbers and simple ratios sound more natural, while decimal numbers and complex ratios sound metallic. A number may be added afterwards to control the harmonicity of any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmh2)
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmh("<1 2 1.5 1.61>")
._scope()

name: fmi
summary: Sets the Frequency Modulation of the synth. Controls the modulation index, which defines the brightness of the sound. A number may be added afterwards to control the modulation index of any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fm3). Also, FMs may be routed into each other with matrix commands like fm13, which would send fm1 back into fm3
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm("<0 1 2 8 32>")
._scope()

name: fmrelease
summary: Release time for the FM envelope: how much modulation is applied after the note is released A number may be added afterwards to control the release of the envelope of any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmrel8)

name: fmsustain
summary: Sustain level for the FM envelope: how much modulation is applied after the decay phase A number may be added afterwards to control the sustain of the envelope of any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmsus7)
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmdecay(.1)
.fmsustain("<1 .75 .5 0>")
._scope()

name: fmwave
summary: Waveform of the fm modulator A number may be added afterwards to control the waveform any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmwave6)

name: focus
summary: Similar to compress, but doesn't leave gaps, and the 'focus' can be bigger than a cycle

name: fold
summary: Wavefolding distortion

name: freq
summary: Set frequency of sound.

name: fromBipolar
summary: Assumes a numerical pattern, containing bipolar values in the range -1 .. 1 Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the unipolar range 0 .. 1

name: ftype
summary: Sets the filter type. The ladder filter is more aggressive. More types might be added in the future.
examples: note("{f g g c d a a#}%8").s("sawtooth").lpenv(4).lpf(500).ftype("<0 1 2>").lpq(1)

note("c f g g a c d4").fast(2)
.sound('sawtooth')
.lpf(200).fanchor(0)
.lpenv(3).lpq(1)
.ftype("<ladder 12db 24db>")

name: FX
summary: Establishes an FX chain. Can be called by chaining .FX(fx1).FX(fx2).. calls and/or in a single .FX(fx1, fx2, ..) call. The fx1, .. are _patterns_ which establish the controls of the given effect. See examples.
examples:
$: s("[sbd <hh [bd | lt | oh]>]*4").dec(.4)
  .FX(
    phaser(0.5).gain(2),
    bpf(800),
    distort(1.3),
    room(0.2),
    delay(0.5).gain(1.25),
    distort(0.3),
  ).fxr(1.7) // sets release time of effects (like delay)

$: s("saw").fm(0.5)
  .delay(0.3) // outer effects are applied *last*
  .FX(coarse(4)) // first coarse
  .FX(lpf(500).lpe(4).lpa(1).lpd(2)) // then lpf
  .FX(distort(1)) // then distort

name: gain
summary: Controls the gain by an exponential amount.

name: gap
summary: Does absolutely nothing, but with a given metrical 'steps'

name: grow
summary: *Experimental* Progressively grows the pattern by 'n' steps until the full pattern is played, or if a second value is given (using mininotation list syntax with :), that number of times. A positive number will progressively grow steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

name: hard
summary: Hard-clipping distortion

name: hpattack
summary: Sets the attack duration for the highpass filter envelope.

name: hpdc
summary: DC offset of the LFO for the highpass filter

name: hpdecay
summary: Sets the decay duration for the highpass filter envelope.

name: hpdepth
summary: Depth of the LFO for the highpass filter

name: hpdepthfrequency
summary: Depth of the LFO for the hipass filter, in hz

name: hpenv
summary: Sets the highpass filter envelope modulation depth.

name: hpf
summary: Applies the cutoff frequency of the high-pass filter. When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'hpq' parameter, separated by ':'.

name: hpq
summary: Controls the high-pass q-value.

name: hprate
summary: Rate of the LFO for the highpass filter

name: hprelease
summary: Sets the release time for the highpass filter envelope.

name: hpshape
summary: Shape of the LFO for the highpass filter

name: hpskew
summary: Skew of the LFO for the highpass filter

name: hpsustain
summary: Sets the sustain amplitude for the highpass filter envelope.

name: hpsync
summary: Cycle-synced rate of the LFO for the highpass filter

name: hurry
summary: Both speeds up the pattern (like 'fast') and the sample playback (like 'speed').

name: inhabit
summary: Picks patterns (or plain values) either from a list (by index) or a lookup table (by name). Similar to pick, but cycles are squeezed into the target ('inhabited') pattern.

name: inhabitmod
summary: The same as inhabit, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list, it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value. For example, if you pick the fifth pattern of a list of three, you'll get the second one.

name: inside
summary: Carries out an operation 'inside' a cycle.

name: into
summary: Breaks a pattern into pieces according to the structure of a given pattern. True values in the given pattern cause the corresponding subcycle of the source pattern to be looped, and for an (optional) given function to be applied. False values result in the corresponding part of the source pattern to be played unchanged.

name: invert
summary: Swaps 1s and 0s in a binary pattern.

name: irand
summary: A continuous pattern of random integers, between 0 and n-1.
examples:
// randomly select scale notes from 0 - 7 (= C to C)
n(irand(8)).struct("x x*2 x x*3").scale("C:minor")

name: irbegin
summary: Sets the beginning of the IR response sample

name: iresponse
summary: Sets the sample to use as an impulse response for the reverb.

name: irspeed
summary: Sets speed of the sample for the impulse response.

name: isaw
summary: A sawtooth signal between 1 and 0 (like saw, but flipped).

name: isaw2
summary: A sawtooth signal between 1 and -1 (like saw2, but flipped).

name: iter
summary: Divides a pattern into a given number of subdivisions, plays the subdivisions in order, but increments the starting subdivision each cycle. The pattern wraps to the first subdivision after the last subdivision is played.

name: iterBack
summary: Like iter, but plays the subdivisions in reverse order. Known as iter' in tidalcycles

name: itri
summary: An inverted triangle signal between 1 and 0 (like tri, but flipped).

name: itri2
summary: An inverted triangle signal between -1 and 1 (like itri, but bipolar).

name: jux
summary: The jux function creates strange stereo effects, by applying a function to a pattern, but only in the right-hand channel.
examples: s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").jux(rev)
s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").jux(press)
s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").jux(iter(4))

name: juxBy
summary: Jux with adjustable stereo width. 0 = mono, 1 = full stereo.
examples: s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").juxBy("<0 .5 1>/2", rev)

name: K
summary: Produces a [Kabelsalat](https://kabel.salat.dev/) modular sound engine. This can be used as either an effect (by including audioin() at the beginning of your kabel expression) or as a sound source (via any expression which doesn't start with audioin()). Some helpers you have available to you: * Strudel mini notation works fine in K(..) via "" or ` * More complex Strudel expressions (like "0 1 2".fast(4) or irand(24)) can be written by wrapping them in S(..) inside your Kabel code * We expose Strudel's note frequency under sFreq and Strudel's gate information under sGate * You can use more complex multi-line expressions (like let x = a; let y = b; x.lpf(y);`) by wrapping them inside a function in K (see example).
examples:
note("A c e".fast(4)).transpose("<0 2 4 6 8>")
  .scale("F:minor").transpose("12")
  .s("saw")
  .K(
    // audioin().mul(sGate.adsr(0.001, 0.3, 0, 0.2)) // as effect
    saw(saw(sFreq / "2!3 16").mul(8).add(sFreq).lag("0!3 0.1")).mul(0.3) // as source
    .mul(sGate.adsr(0, 0.15, 0.5, "0.1!3 1"))
    .lpf(sGate.adsr(0, 0.2, 0.3, 0.2).mul(1).add(0))
    .add(x => x.delay(S("0.3 0.2".fast(2))).mul(0.7))
    .add(x => x.delay("0.03 [0.08 0.01] 0.01 0.013").mul(0.77)).mul(0.7)
    .add(x => x.delay(.13).mul(0.7))
    .out()
  )

name: keyDown
summary: returns true when a key or array of keys is held [Key name reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/UI_Events/Keyboard_event_key_values)

name: label
summary: Sets the displayed text for an event on the pianoroll

name: lastOf
summary: Applies the given function every n cycles, starting from the last cycle.

name: late
summary: Nudge a pattern to start later in time. Equivalent of Tidal's ~> operator

name: layer
summary: Layers the result of the given function(s). Like superimpose, but without the original pattern:

name: leslie
summary: Emulation of a Leslie speaker: speakers rotating in a wooden amplified cabinet.

name: lfo
summary: Configures an LFO. Can be called in sequence like pat.lfo(...).lfo(...) to set up multiple LFOs. There are two ways to declare which control will be modulated: 1. Explicitly put control in the config (e.g. lfo({ c: "lpf" })) 2. If the control parameter is absent, the control _immediately before_ the lfo call will be used (e.g. s("saw").lpf(500).lfo() to modulate lpf) Modulators can be referred to by id so that they can be updated later e.g. inside a sometimes. See example below.

name: linger
summary: Selects the given fraction of the pattern and repeats that part to fill the remainder of the cycle.

name: lock
summary: Specifies whether delaytime is calculated relative to cps.

name: log
summary: Writes the content of the current event to the console (visible in the side menu).

name: logValues
summary: A simplified version of log which writes all "values" (various configurable parameters) within the event to the console (visible in the side menu).

name: loop
summary: Loops the sample. Note that the tempo of the loop is not synced with the cycle tempo. To change the loop region, use loopBegin / loopEnd.

name: loopAt
summary: Makes the sample fit the given number of cycles by changing the speed.

name: loopAtCps
summary: Makes the sample fit the given number of cycles and cps value, by changing the speed. Please note that at some point cps will be given by a global clock and this function will be deprecated/removed.

name: loopBegin
summary: Begin to loop at a specific point in the sample (inbetween begin and end). Note that the loop point must be inbetween begin and end, and before loopEnd! Note: Samples starting with wt_ will automatically loop! (wt = wavetable)

name: loopEnd
summary: End the looping section at a specific point in the sample (inbetween begin and end). Note that the loop point must be inbetween begin and end, and after loopBegin!

name: lpattack
summary: Sets the attack duration for the lowpass filter envelope.

name: lpdc
summary: DC offset of the LFO for the lowpass filter

name: lpdecay
summary: Sets the decay duration for the lowpass filter envelope.

name: lpdepth
summary: Depth of the LFO for the lowpass filter

name: lpdepthfrequency
summary: Depth of the LFO for the lowpass filter, in HZ

name: lpenv
summary: Sets the lowpass filter envelope modulation depth.

name: lpf
summary: Applies the cutoff frequency of the low-pass filter. When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'lpq' parameter, separated by ':'.

name: lpq
summary: Controls the low-pass q-value.

name: lprate
summary: Rate of the LFO for the lowpass filter

name: lprelease
summary: Sets the release time for the lowpass filter envelope.

name: lpshape
summary: Shape of the LFO for the lowpass filter

name: lpskew
summary: Skew of the LFO for the lowpass filter

name: lpsustain
summary: Sets the sustain amplitude for the lowpass filter envelope.

name: lpsync
summary: Cycle-synced rate of the LFO for the lowpass filter

name: lrate
summary: Rate of modulation / rotation for leslie effect

name: lsize
summary: Physical size of the cabinet in meters. Be careful, it might be slightly larger than your computer. Affects the Doppler amount (pitch warble)

name: midibend
summary: MIDI pitch bend: Sends a MIDI pitch bend message.

name: midichan
summary: MIDI channel: Sets the MIDI channel for the event.

name: midicmd
summary: MIDI command: Sends a MIDI command message.

name: midiport
summary: MIDI port: Sets the MIDI port for the event.

name: miditouch
summary: MIDI key after touch: Sends a MIDI key after touch message.

name: mode
summary: Remove anchor note from the voicing. Useful for melody harmonization

name: morph
summary: Takes two binary rhythms represented as lists of 1s and 0s, and a number between 0 and 1 that morphs between them. The two lists should contain the same number of true values.

name: mousex
summary: The mouse's x position value ranges from 0 to 1.

name: mousey
summary: The mouse's y position value ranges from 0 to 1.

name: n
summary: Selects the given index from the sample map. Numbers too high will wrap around. n can also be used to play midi numbers, but it is recommended to use note instead.

name: never
summary: Shorthand for .sometimesBy(0, fn) (never calls fn)

name: noise
summary: Adds pink noise to the mix

name: note
summary: Plays the given note name or midi number. A note name consists of - a letter (a-g or A-G) - optional accidentals (b or #) - optional (possibly negative) octave number (0-9). Defaults to 3 Examples of valid note names: c, bb, Bb, f#, c3, A4, Eb2, c#5 You can also use midi numbers instead of note names, where 69 is mapped to A4 440Hz in 12EDO.

name: nrpnn
summary: MIDI NRPN non-registered parameter number: Sends a MIDI NRPN non-registered parameter number message.

name: nrpv
summary: MIDI NRPN non-registered parameter value: Sends a MIDI NRPN non-registered parameter value message.

name: octave
summary: Sets the default octave of a synth.

name: octaves
summary: How many octaves are voicing steps spread apart, defaults to 1 @name octaves @param {number | Pattern} count the number of octaves @example chord("<Am C D F Am E Am E>").octaves("<2 4>").voicing()

name: off
summary: Superimposes the function result on top of the original pattern, delayed by the given time.

name: offset
summary: Sets how the voicing is offset from the anchored position
examples: chord("<Am C D F Am E Am E>").offset("<0 1 2 3 4 5>") // alter the voicing each time

name: often
summary: Shorthand for .sometimesBy(0.75, fn)

name: onsetsOnly
summary: Returns a new pattern, with all haps without onsets filtered out. A hap with an onset is one with a whole timespan that begins at the same time as its part timespan.

name: onTriggerTime
summary: make something happen on event time uses browser timeout which is innacurate for audio tasks

name: orbit
summary: An orbit is a global parameter context for patterns. Patterns with the same orbit will share the same global effects.

name: oschost
summary: The host to send open sound control messages to. Requires running the OSC bridge.

name: oscport
summary: The port to send open sound control messages to. Requires running the OSC bridge.

name: outside
summary: Carries out an operation 'outside' a cycle.

name: pace
summary: *Experimental* Speeds a pattern up or down, to fit to the given number of steps per cycle.
examples:
sound("bd sd cp").pace(4)
// The same as sound("{bd sd cp}%4") or sound("<bd sd cp>*4")

name: palindrome
summary: Applies rev to a pattern every other cycle, so that the pattern alternates between forwards and backwards.

name: pan
summary: Sets position in stereo.
examples: s("bd rim sd rim bd ~ cp rim").pan(sine.slow(2))

name: panchor
summary: Sets the range anchor of the envelope: - anchor 0: range = [note, note + penv] - anchor 1: range = [note - penv, note] If you don't set an anchor, the value will default to the psustain value.

name: parray
summary: Turns a list of patterns into a single pattern which outputs list-values

name: partials
summary: Scale the magnitude of the harmonics of one of the core synths ('sine', 'tri', 'saw', ..) Can also be used to create a new synth via s('user').partials(...)

name: pattack
summary: Attack time of pitch envelope.

name: pcurve
summary: Curve of envelope. Defaults to linear. exponential is good for kicks

name: pdecay
summary: Decay time of pitch envelope.

name: penv
summary: Amount of pitch envelope. Negative values will flip the envelope. If you don't set other pitch envelope controls, pattack:.2 will be the default.

name: per
summary: A pattern measuring the 'shortness' of events, or in other words, the duration of pattern events, in events per cycle. per doesn't have structure itself, but takes structure, and therefore event durations, from the pattern that it is combined with. For example per.struct("1 1 [1 1] 1") would give the same as "4 4 [8 8] 4". See also its reciprocal, cyclesPer.

name: perlin
summary: Generates a continuous pattern of [perlin noise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perlin_noise), in the range 0..1.

name: perx
summary: Like per but measures the shortness of events according to an exponential curve. In particular, where the event duration halves, the returned value increases by one. perx.struct("1 1 [1 [1 1]] 1") would therefore be the same as "3 3 [4 [5 5]] 3".

name: phaser
summary: Phaser audio effect that approximates popular guitar pedals.

name: phasercenter
summary: The center frequency of the phaser in HZ. Defaults to 1000

name: phaserdepth
summary: The amount the signal is affected by the phaser effect. Defaults to 0.75

name: phasersweep
summary: The frequency sweep range of the lfo for the phaser effect. Defaults to 2000

name: phases
summary: Rotates the harmonics of one of the core synths ('sine', 'tri', 'saw', 'user', ..) by a list of phases

name: pick
summary: Picks patterns (or plain values) either from a list (by index) or a lookup table (by name). Similar to inhabit, but maintains the structure of the original patterns.
examples: note("<0 1 2!2 3>".pick(["g a", "e f", "f g f g" , "g c d"]))

name: pickF
summary: pickF lets you use a pattern of numbers to pick which function to apply to another pattern.

name: pickmod
summary: The same as pick, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list, it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value. For example, if you pick the fifth pattern of a list of three, you'll get the second one.

name: pickmodF
summary: The same as pickF, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the functions list, it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.

name: pickmodOut
summary: The same as pickOut, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list, it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.

name: pickmodReset
summary: The same as pickReset, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list, it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.

name: pickmodRestart
summary: The same as pickRestart, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list, it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.

name: pickOut
summary: Similar to pick, but it applies an outerJoin instead of an innerJoin.

name: pickReset
summary: Similar to pick, but the choosen pattern is reset when its index is triggered.

name: pickRestart
summary: Similar to pick, but the choosen pattern is restarted when its index is triggered.

name: ply
summary: The ply function repeats each event the given number of times.

name: plyForEach
summary: The plyForEach function repeats each event the given number of times, applying the given function to each event. This version of ply uses the iteration index as an argument to the function, similar to echoWith.

name: plyWith
summary: The plyWith function repeats each event the given number of times, applying the given function to each event.\n

name: polymeter
summary: *Experimental* Aligns the steps of the patterns, creating polymeters. The patterns are repeated until they all fit the cycle. For example, in the below the first pattern is repeated twice, and the second is repeated three times, to fit the lowest common multiple of six steps.
examples:
// The same as note("{c eb g, c2 g2}%6")
polymeter("c eb g", "c2 g2").note()

name: polyrhythm
summary: Restarts the pattern for each onset of the restart pattern. While reset will only reset the current cycle, restart will start from cycle 0.

name: postgain
summary: Gain applied after all effects have been processed.

name: prelease
summary: Release time of pitch envelope
examples:
note("<c eb g bb> ~")
.release(.5) // to hear the pitch release
.prelease("<0 .1 .25 .5>")

name: press
summary: Syncopates a rhythm, by shifting each event halfway into its timespan.

name: pressBy
summary: Like press, but allows you to specify the amount by which each event is shifted. pressBy(0.5) is the same as press, while pressBy(1/3) shifts each event by a third of its timespan.

name: progNum
summary: MIDI program number: Sends a MIDI program change message.

name: pure
summary: A discrete value that repeats once per cycle.

name: pw
summary: Controls the pulsewidth of the pulse oscillator

name: pwrate
summary: Controls the lfo rate for the pulsewidth of the pulse oscillator

name: pwsweep
summary: Controls the lfo sweep for the pulsewidth of the pulse oscillator

name: queryArc
summary: Query haps inside the given time span.

name: rand
summary: A continuous pattern of random numbers, between 0 and 1.

name: rand2
summary: A continuous pattern of random numbers, between -1 and 1

name: randL
summary: Creates a list of random numbers of the given length

name: range
summary: Assumes a numerical pattern, containing unipolar values in the range 0 .. 1. Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the given min/max range. Most useful in combination with continuous patterns.

name: range2
summary: Assumes a numerical pattern, containing bipolar values in the range -1 .. 1 Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the given min/max range.

name: rangex
summary: Assumes a numerical pattern, containing unipolar values in the range 0 .. 1 Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the given min/max range, following an exponential curve.

name: rarely
summary: Shorthand for .sometimesBy(0.25, fn)

name: ratio
summary: Allows dividing numbers via list notation using ":". Returns a new pattern with just numbers.

name: ref
summary: exposes a custom value at query time. basically allows mutating state without evaluation

name: register
summary: Registers a new pattern method. The method is added to the Pattern class + the standalone function is returned from register.

name: release
summary: Amplitude envelope release time: The time it takes after the offset to go from sustain level to zero.

name: removeUndefineds
summary: Returns a new pattern, with haps containing undefined values removed from query results.

name: repeatCycles
summary: Repeats each cycle the given number of times.

name: replicate
summary: *Experimental* replicate is similar to fast in that it increases its density, but it also increases the step count accordingly. So stepcat("a b".replicate(2), "c d") would be the same as "a b a b c d", whereas stepcat("a b".fast(2), "c d") would be the same as "[a b] [a b] c d". TODO: find out how this function differs from extend
examples:
stepcat(
  sound("bd bd - cp").replicate(2),
  sound("bd - sd -")
).pace(8)

name: rev
summary: Reverse all cycles in a pattern. See also revv for reversing a whole pattern.

name: revv
summary: Reverse a whole pattern. See also rev for reversing each cycle.

name: ribbon
summary: Loops the pattern inside an offset for cycles. If you think of the entire span of time in cycles as a ribbon, you can cut a single piece and loop it.

name: room
summary: Sets the level of reverb. When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'size' parameter, separated by ':'.

name: roomdim
summary: Reverb lowpass frequency at -60dB (in hertz). When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

name: roomfade
summary: Reverb fade time (in seconds). When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

name: roomlp
summary: Reverb lowpass starting frequency (in hertz). When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

name: roomsize
summary: Sets the room size of the reverb, see room. When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

name: round
summary: Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values rounded to the nearest integer.

name: run
summary: A discrete pattern of numbers from 0 to n-1

name: s
summary: Select a sound / sample by name. When using mininotation, you can also optionally supply 'n' and 'gain' parameters separated by ':'.

name: saw
summary: A sawtooth signal between 0 and 1.

name: saw2
summary: A sawtooth signal between -1 and 1 (like saw, but bipolar).

name: scramble
summary: Slices a pattern into the given number of parts, then plays those parts at random. Similar to shuffle, but parts might be played more than once, or not at all, per cycle.

name: scrub
summary: Allows you to scrub an audio file like a tape loop by passing values that represents the position in the audio file in the optional array syntax ex: "0.5:2", the second value controls the speed of playback

name: seed
summary: Change the seed for random signals. Normally, random signals depend on time, so two patterns at the same time will have the same random values. Specifying a new seed changes the signal output by rand. This also affects other functions that use randomness, like shuffle and sometimes.
examples:
$: s("hh*4").degrade();
$: s("bd*4").degrade().seed(1); // Will degrade different events from the hi-hat

name: segment
summary: Samples the pattern at a rate of n events per cycle. Useful for turning a continuous pattern into a discrete one.

name: seq
summary: Like cat, but the items are crammed into one cycle.

name: seqPLoop
summary: Similarly to arrange, allows you to arrange multiple patterns together over multiple cycles. Unlike arrange, you specify a start and stop time for each pattern rather than duration, which means that patterns can overlap.

name: sequence
summary: See fastcat

name: sequenceP
summary: Takes a list of patterns, and returns a pattern of lists.

name: setContext
summary: Returns a new pattern with the context field set to every hap set to the given value.

name: shape
summary: (Deprecated) Wave shaping distortion. WARNING: can suddenly get unpredictably loud. Please use distort instead, which has a more predictable response curve second option in optional array syntax (ex: ".9:.5") applies a postgain to the output

name: shrink
summary: *Experimental* Progressively shrinks the pattern by 'n' steps until there's nothing left, or if a second value is given (using mininotation list syntax with :), that number of times. A positive number will progressively drop steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

name: shuffle
summary: Slices a pattern into the given number of parts, then plays those parts in random order. Each part will be played exactly once per cycle.

name: silence
summary: Does absolutely nothing..

name: sine
summary: A sine signal between 0 and 1.

name: sine2
summary: A sine signal between -1 and 1 (like sine, but bipolar).

name: sinefold
summary: Wavefolding distortion composed with sinusoid

name: slice
summary: Chops samples into the given number of slices, triggering those slices with a given pattern of slice numbers. Instead of a number, it also accepts a list of numbers from 0 to 1 to slice at specific points.

name: slow
summary: Slow down a pattern over the given number of cycles. Like the "/" operator in mini notation.
examples: s("bd hh sd hh").slow(2) // s("[bd hh sd hh]/2")

name: slowcat
summary: Concatenation: combines a list of patterns, switching between them successively, one per cycle.

name: slowcatPrime
summary: Concatenation: combines a list of patterns, switching between them successively, one per cycle. Unlike slowcat, this version will skip cycles.

name: soft
summary: Soft-clipping distortion

name: someCycles
summary: Shorthand for .someCyclesBy(0.5, fn)

name: someCyclesBy
summary: Randomly applies the given function by the given probability on a cycle by cycle basis. Similar to sometimesBy

name: sometimes
summary: Applies the given function with a 50% chance

name: sometimesBy
summary: Randomly applies the given function by the given probability. Similar to someCyclesBy

name: sortHapsByPart
summary: Returns a new pattern, which returns haps sorted in temporal order. Mainly of use when comparing two patterns for equality, in tests.

name: source
summary: Define a custom webaudio node to use as a sound source.

name: speed
summary: Changes the speed of sample playback, i.e. a cheap way of changing pitch.

name: splice
summary: Works the same as slice, but changes the playback speed of each slice to match the duration of its step.

name: splitQueries
summary: Returns a new pattern, with queries split at cycle boundaries. This makes some calculations easier to express, as all haps are then constrained to happen within a cycle.

name: spread
summary: Set the stereo pan spread for supported oscillators
examples: note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").spread("<0 .3 1>")

name: square
summary: A square signal between 0 and 1.

name: square2
summary: A square signal between -1 and 1 (like square, but bipolar).

name: squeeze
summary: Pick from the list of values (or patterns of values) via the index using the given pattern of integers. The selected pattern will be compressed to fit the duration of the selecting event
examples: note(squeeze("<0@2 [1!2] 2>", ["g a", "f g f g" , "g a c d"]))

name: squiz
summary: Made by Calum Gunn. Reminiscent of some weird mixture of filter, ring-modulator and pitch-shifter. The SuperCollider manual defines Squiz as: "A simplistic pitch-raising algorithm. It's not meant to sound natural; its sound is reminiscent of some weird mixture of filter, ring-modulator and pitch-shifter, depending on the input. The algorithm works by cutting the signal into fragments (delimited by upwards-going zero-crossings) and squeezing those fragments in the time domain (i.e. simply playing them back faster than they came in), leaving silences inbetween. All the parameters apart from memlen can be modulated."

name: stack
summary: The given items are played at the same time at the same length.

name: stepalt
summary: *Experimental* Concatenates patterns stepwise, according to an inferred 'steps per cycle'. Similar to stepcat, but if an argument is a list, the whole pattern will alternate between the elements in the list.
examples:
stepalt(["bd cp", "mt"], "bd").sound()
// The same as "bd cp bd mt bd".sound()

name: stepcat
summary: 'Concatenates' patterns like fastcat, but proportional to a number of steps per cycle. The steps can either be inferred from the pattern, or provided as a [length, pattern] pair. Has the alias timecat.
examples:
stepcat("bd sd cp","hh hh").sound()
// the same as "bd sd cp hh hh".sound()

name: stretch
summary: Changes the speed of sample playback, i.e. a cheap way of changing pitch.

name: striate
summary: Cuts each sample into the given number of parts, triggering progressive portions of each sample at each loop.

name: stripContext
summary: Returns a new pattern with the context field of every hap set to an empty object.

name: stut
summary: Deprecated. Like echo, but the last 2 parameters are flipped.

name: superimpose
summary: Superimposes the result of the given function(s) on top of the original pattern:

name: sustain
summary: Amplitude envelope sustain level: The level which is reached after attack / decay, being sustained until the offset.

name: swing
summary: Shorthand for swingBy with 1/3:

name: swingBy
summary: The function swingBy x n breaks each cycle into n slices, and then delays events in the second half of each slice by the amount x, which is relative to the size of the (half) slice. So if x is 0 it does nothing, 0.5 delays for half the note duration, and 1 will wrap around to doing nothing again. The end result is a shuffle or swing-like rhythm

name: sysex
summary: MIDI sysex: Sends a MIDI sysex message.

name: sysexdata
summary: MIDI sysex data: Sends a MIDI sysex message.

name: sysexid
summary: MIDI sysex ID: Sends a MIDI sysex identifier message.

name: tag
summary: Tags each Hap with an identifier. Good for filtering. The function populates Hap.context.tags (Array).
examples:
s("saw!16").note("F1")
  .lpf(tri.range(40, 80).slow(4)).lpenv(5).lpq(4).lpd(0.15)
  .when(rand.late(0.1).gte(0.5), x => x.transpose("12").tag('altered'))
  .when(rand.late(0.2).gte(0.5), x => x.s("square").tag('altered'))
  .when("<0 1>", x => x.filter((hap) => hap.hasTag('altered')))

name: take
summary: *Experimental* Takes the given number of steps from a pattern (dropping the rest). A positive number will take steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.
examples:
"bd cp ht mt".take("2").sound()
// The same as "bd cp".sound()

"bd cp ht mt".take("1 2 3").sound()
// The same as "bd bd cp bd cp ht".sound()

"bd cp ht mt".take("-1 -2 -3").sound()
// The same as "mt ht mt cp ht mt".sound()

name: time
summary: A signal representing the cycle time.

name: timecat
summary: Aliases for stepcat

name: toBipolar
summary: Assumes a numerical pattern, containing unipolar values in the range 0 .. 1. Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the bipolar range -1 .. 1

name: tour
summary: *Experimental* Inserts a pattern into a list of patterns. On the first repetition it will be inserted at the end of the list, then moved backwards through the list on successive repetitions. The patterns are added together stepwise, with all repetitions taking place over a single cycle. Using pace to set the number of steps per cycle is therefore usually recommended.
examples:
"[c g]".tour("e f", "e f g", "g f e c").note()
   .sound("folkharp")
   .pace(8)

name: transient
summary: Transient shaper. Gives independent control over the emphasis on transients and sustains

name: tremolo
summary: Modulate the amplitude of a sound with a continuous waveform

name: tremolodepth
summary: Depth of amplitude modulation

name: tremolophase
summary: Alter the phase of the modulation waveform

name: tremoloshape
summary: Shape of amplitude modulation
examples: note("{f g c d}%16").tremsync(4).tremoloshape("<sine tri square>").s("sawtooth")

name: tremoloskew
summary: Alter the shape of the modulation waveform

name: tremolosync
summary: Modulate the amplitude of a sound with a continuous waveform

name: tri
summary: A triangle signal between 0 and 1.

name: tri2
summary: A triangle signal between -1 and 1 (like tri, but bipolar).

name: undegrade
summary: Inverse of degrade: Randomly removes 50% of events from the pattern. Shorthand for .undegradeBy(0.5) Events that would be removed by degrade are let through by undegrade and vice versa (see second example).

name: undegradeBy
summary: Inverse of degradeBy: Randomly removes events from the pattern by a given amount. 0 = 100% chance of removal 1 = 0% chance of removal Events that would be removed by degradeBy are let through by undegradeBy and vice versa (see second example).

name: unison
summary: Set number of stacked voices for supported oscillators
examples: note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").unison("<1 2 7>")

name: unit
summary: Used in conjunction with speed, accepts values of "r" (rate, default behavior), "c" (cycles), or "s" (seconds). Using unit "c" means speed will be interpreted in units of cycles, e.g. speed "1" means samples will be stretched to fill a cycle. Using unit "s" means the playback speed will be adjusted so that the duration is the number of seconds specified by speed.

name: useRNG
summary: Sets which random number generator to use. Historically Strudel would use useRNG('legacy'), which remains the default. To use a new more statistically precise RNG, try useRNG('precise').

name: velocity
summary: Sets the velocity from 0 to 1. Is multiplied together with gain.

name: vib
summary: Applies a vibrato to the frequency of the oscillator.
examples:
// change the modulation depth with ":"
note("a e")
.vib("<.5 1 2 4 8 16>:12")
._scope()

name: vibmod
summary: Sets the vibrato depth in semitones. Only has an effect if vibrato | vib | v is is also set
examples:
// change the vibrato frequency with ":"
note("a e")
.vibmod("<.25 .5 1 2 12>:8")
._scope()

name: vowel
summary: Formant filter to make things sound like vowels.
examples: s("bd sd mt ht bd [~ cp] ht lt").vowel("[a|e|i|o|u]")

name: warp
summary: Amount of warp (alteration of the waveform) to apply to the wavetable oscillator

name: warpattack
summary: Attack time of the wavetable oscillator's warp envelope

name: warpdc
summary: DC offset of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's warp

name: warpdecay
summary: Decay time of the wavetable oscillator's warp envelope

name: warpdepth
summary: Depth of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's warp

name: warpenv
summary: Amount of envelope applied wavetable oscillator's position envelope

name: warpmode
summary: Type of warp (alteration of the waveform) to apply to the wavetable oscillator. The current options are: none, asym, bendp, bendm, bendmp, sync, quant, fold, pwm, orbit, spin, chaos, primes, binary, brownian, reciprocal, wormhole, logistic, sigmoid, fractal, flip
examples:
s("morgana").bank("wt_digital").seg(8).note("F1").warp("0 0.25 0.5 0.75 1")
  .warpmode("<asym bendp spin logistic sync wormhole brownian>*2")

name: warprate
summary: Rate of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's warp

name: warprelease
summary: Release time of the wavetable oscillator's warp envelope

name: warpshape
summary: Shape of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's warp

name: warpskew
summary: Skew of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's warp

name: warpsustain
summary: Sustain time of the wavetable oscillator's warp envelope

name: warpsync
summary: cycle synced rate of the LFO for the wavetable warp position

name: wchoose
summary: Chooses randomly from the given list of elements by giving a probability to each element

name: wchooseCycles
summary: Picks one of the elements at random each cycle by giving a probability to each element
examples: wchooseCycles(["c c c",5], ["a a a",3], ["f f f",1]).fast(4).note()

// The probability can itself be a pattern
wchooseCycles(["bd(3,8)","<5 0>"], ["hh hh hh",3]).fast(4).s()

name: when
summary: Applies the given function whenever the given pattern is in a true state.

name: whenKey
summary: Do something on a keypress, or array of keypresses [Key name reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/UI_Events/Keyboard_event_key_values)

name: withContext
summary: Returns a new pattern with the given function applied to the context field of every hap.

name: withHap
summary: As with withHaps, but applies the function to every hap, rather than every list of haps.

name: withHaps
summary: Returns a new pattern with the given function applied to the list of haps returned by every query.

name: withHapSpan
summary: Similar to withQuerySpan, but the function is applied to the timespans of all haps returned by pattern queries (both part timespans, and where present, whole timespans).

name: withHapTime
summary: As with withHapSpan, but the function is applied to both the begin and end time of the hap timespans.

name: within
summary: Use within to apply a function to only a part of a pattern.

name: withLoc
summary: Returns a new pattern with the given location information added to the context of every hap.

name: withQuerySpan
summary: Returns a new pattern, where the given function is applied to the query timespan before passing it to the original pattern.

name: withQueryTime
summary: As with withQuerySpan, but the function is applied to both the begin and end time of the query timespan.

name: withSeed
summary: Modify a pattern by applying a function to the randomSeed control if present

name: withValue
summary: Returns a new pattern, with the function applied to the value of each hap. It has the alias fmap.

name: worklet
summary: Creates a worklet effect. Typically derived by writing K(...) in the REPL which will parse Kabelsalat code.

name: wt
summary: Position in the wavetable of the wavetable oscillator

name: wtattack
summary: Attack time of the wavetable oscillator's position envelope

name: wtdc
summary: DC offset of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

name: wtdecay
summary: Decay time of the wavetable oscillator's position envelope

name: wtdepth
summary: Depth of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

name: wtenv
summary: Amount of envelope applied wavetable oscillator's position envelope

name: wtphaserand
summary: Amount of randomness of the initial phase of the wavetable oscillator.

name: wtrate
summary: Rate of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

name: wtrelease
summary: Release time of the wavetable oscillator's position envelope

name: wtshape
summary: Shape of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

name: wtskew
summary: Skew of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

name: wtsustain
summary: Sustain time of the wavetable oscillator's position envelope

name: wtsync
summary: cycle synced rate of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

name: xfade
summary: Cross-fades between left and right from 0 to 1: - 0 = (full left, no right) - .5 = (both equal) - 1 = (no left, full right)

name: zip
summary: *Experimental* 'zips' together the steps of the provided patterns. This can create a long repetition, taking place over a single, dense cycle. Using pace to set the number of steps per cycle is therefore usually recommended.
examples:
zip("e f", "e f g", "g [f e] a f4 c").note()
   .sound("folkharp")
   .pace(8)

name: zoom
summary: Plays a portion of a pattern, specified by the beginning and end of a time span. The new resulting pattern is played over the time period of the original pattern:
examples:
s("bd*2 hh*3 [sd bd]*2 perc").zoom(0.25, 0.75)
// s("hh*3 [sd bd]*2") // equivalent
